title: add profiling baselines, representative workload runners, and reporting pipeline v31
author: Priya Patel
body:
Motivation: The benchmark lab needs an updated set of profiling baselines and representative workload runners to better capture current inference traffic patterns and provide stable inputs for the reporting pipeline. This PR bundles three related efforts: (1) new profiling baseline definitions for cold/warm start and mixed-sequence workloads, (2) new representative workload runners that exercise KV-cache heavy long-context and short-chat scenarios, and (3) an updated reporting pipeline that aggregates runner results and emits per-model profiling artifacts to the central metrics bucket.

Summary of changes: 1) profiles/baselines: added v31 baselines (cold_start_64, warm_start_512, mixed_sequence) plus JSON schemas and validation. 2) runners/representative: added two new runners (kv_cache_long_context_runner, short_chat_runner) with config-driven knobs for batch sizing, prefix-caching, and synthetic-user pacing. 3) reporting/pipeline: new aggregation job (reporting/aggregate_profiling_v2.py) which normalizes token-level timing, computes p50/p95/p99 latency histograms, and emits compressed artifacts and a summary CSV for downstream dashboards. 4) infra/ci: added a lightweight smoke job that runs the new runners on an infra-playback fixture (fast-mode) to catch integration regressions in PRs.

Testing and validation: - Unit tests for baseline validation and runner config parsing added. - End-to-end smoke integration runs in CI (fast-mode) passed; a full nightly profiling job passed on staging. - Local microbench: compared v30 -> v31 baselines; p50 improved ~3% for long-context runs due to batching improvements applied in a follow-up commit.

Checklist: - [x] Add baseline definitions and schemas - [x] Implement runner harness and example configs - [x] Update reporting pipeline and add integration tests - [x] Add CI smoke job and documentation note - [x] Add release notes entry

Migration notes: Consumers of baseline artifacts should pick the v31 tag; the reporting pipeline emits a new compressed artifact key (profiling-v31/<model>/<date>/profile.json.gz). Downstream dashboards must be updated to read p50/p95/p99 keys from the new summary CSV (column names unchanged).

Rollout: The change is additive and backwards compatible. The nightly job will publish v31 baselines in staging for one week before we flip production. If downstream consumers need the old format we kept v30 artifacts for 30 days.

Related: ENG-3245 (profiling baseline refresh), ENG-3982 (representative runner expansion).
commits: chore(reporting): add aggregate_profiling_v2.py and CSV summarizer
test(ci): add smoke job for representative runners (fast-mode)
docs: document baseline v31 and reporting artifact keys
fix: small config parsing edge-case in runner harness
review_comments: Alex Chen: Please add a short lived flag to the nightly job so we can roll back quickly if we see regression in production dashboards.
Priya Patel: Added feature flag 'profiling.v31.enable' to the nightly job and defaulted it to false for production. Updated docs to explain toggling.
Mateo Garcia: The CSV summary has a trailing comma when no p99 buckets are present; can you normalize CSV writing to avoid that?
Priya Patel: Fixed CSV writer to always emit consistent columns; added unit test. See commit 'chore(reporting): fix csv writer columns'.
Ruth Kim: Tests look good. One nit: expand comment on cache behaviour in kv_cache_long_context_runner to explain prefix eviction strategy.
Priya Patel: Expanded comment and added a short design note in docs.
release_notes: Add profiling baselines v31, new representative workload runners (kv_cache_long_context, short_chat), and updated reporting pipeline that emits normalized latency histograms and compressed profile artifacts. Nightly job gated by feature flag.
